keyFindings.description: A sentence this change *wrote* is false about the daemon's own behaviour, in a skill an architect reads to know what `child-closed` means. The diff replaces 'session kept and Sandbox `Suspended` with its volume' with 'session kept and the issue's Sandbox deleted with its pod, since it still owes the production check handed to it at the merge'. At a merged close the daemon queues no `IssueSuspend` at all: `internal/workflow/linger.go:82-84` sets `except = claim.RoleImplementer` when `merged`, and `:95-100` enqueues `record.IssueSuspend` only `if !merged`. So nothing deletes the Sandbox at the close — the implementer keeps its pod for the first production-check look, and the deletion follows the look's `pending` report or the check's close, which is what the rest of the same sentence then describes. The old text was wrong in its second half; the new text is wrong in its first, and more confidently. `packages/claude-envoy/legion/skills/legion-architect/SKILL.md:418` carries the same sentence, and `scripts/e2e/stage4b-sandbox-tree.sh:6028` has the matching clause 'the issue's Sandbox with its volume' at the point where the suspension does happen — there only 'with its volume' is wrong, since that Sandbox owns none. Found by the thermonuclear quality pass; verified here against `linger.go` before filing.

The stale-prose class, swept once more under the corrected scope rule — text this change makes false in a file it owns, whether or not the diff touched the line. Verified at this head: `docs/kubernetes.md:5137-5138` says the controller's pod has 'both its containers, the init container and the launcher', where round 4 deleted that init container (`podkind.go:328-334` returns nil); `:5165` tells an operator to read the controller's 'transcript on the volume', where every session is a database row; `internal/supervise/table.go:1113-1118` describes the close as releasing the Sandbox and the volume it owns once every claim has retired, through `store.IssueSuspension`'s release, with the session living on that volume — the retire-wait, the release mode and the file session are all removed by this change, and this is the doc comment on the workflow table's own entry; `internal/podsafety/podsafety.go:62-64` still offers 'files on the issue's volume' as a place Legion puts a session; `internal/runtime/sandbox/names.go:21-27` still describes a volume carried over from an earlier release. The pair also names test comments carrying the file-session rationale (`sandbox/controller_test.go`, `daemon/controller_sweep_test.go`, `supervise/issue_close_test.go`), which I did not verify individually.

Part of the same group, separated because it was a deliberate keep: the unknown-name error still reads `must be 'pvc', 'postgres' or 'cloudsql-iam'`, so an operator who mistypes is told `pvc` is a value this release takes, two lines below the refusal that makes it one it does not. The round-5 census recorded keeping main's text here on purpose, so this is a judgement rather than an oversight and the implementer may argue it: the sibling refusal does explain itself, and the message is main's. My reading is that a list of accepted values should not name a refused one, and `kubernetes_test.go:781-784` pins it either way.

notAFinding.issuePvcs: The quality pass asked for `scripts/e2e/lib/namespace-rig.sh:68-76`'s `issue_pvcs` to be deleted as an orphan this change left, saying the change replaced its callers. That is wrong and I checked rather than forwarded it: `grep -rn issue_pvcs scripts/` finds only its comment and its definition at this head, and `main@origin`'s copy of the file has the same two hits, so it was already callerless before this branch. It is pre-existing dead code with a premise this change happens to contradict — the same adjudication as `production_audit`, and for the same reason: the scope rule is text a change makes false in a file it owns, not every true statement about a file.

roundEightVerification.note: Both round-8 findings are fixed; I verified each at the head.
verified: The stem rule refuses `-*` beside the empty, `.`, `..` and non-plain cases (stage4b-sandbox-tree.sh:1021-1024), with the reason stated in the four lines above it — that every use here quotes and ends its options, and that an option-shaped name is this class's classic shape, so the point of anchoring the destination is not to depend on what a later consumer does. A pod name contains dashes but cannot begin with one, so no legitimate stem is refused.

docs/kubernetes.md:3715-3722 separates the controller's pod, whose Sandbox owns its claim and which does wait on a ReadWriteOnce detach, from an issue pod, which takes no predecessor claim and may instead wait on the predecessor's claim being reaped — the distinction I asked for rather than the deletion.
stage4b-sandbox-tree.sh:3570-3573 says the three PVCs are read by name and owned by their pods, agreeing with the `pod_disk` helper it cites.

testerCountJudgement.position: The tester's downgrade is right and I would not have it quoted as eight. Of the eight failures its suite shows against the previous head's script, only the leading-dash case is a behaviour difference; the other seven fail on the refusal message's wording. A count of negative controls where most differ only in text is the count-answering-a-different-question fault this tree has met all day, and catching it in one's own evidence before anyone quotes it is the right instinct. One control is sufficient here for a reason worth stating: the change is one character added to a character class whose other members are already proven refused by the same code path, so the behaviour under test is the dash alone and a single control exercises exactly it. What should not be said is 'eight controls'; what should be said is 'one behavioural control, and seven cases whose messages moved with it'.
